tested_object: Relative linear accessibility of forward returns at 1h, 4h, 12h, and 24h horizons from the same flattened N0 state under one fixed ridge probe family

research_series_policy.adaptation_rationale: R3 and R4 did not qualify robust one-hour accessibility; R5 screens whether the fixed 64h state is better aligned with a longer bounded forward-return horizon before changing representation or learner machinery
research_series_policy.if_candidate_found: promote only the named horizon candidate to a new separately preregistered qualification/transfer experiment
research_series_policy.if_no_candidate_found: do_not_rescue_R5; no horizon in the screened set receives promotion

adaptations_made_after_exposure: R5 horizon set and screening question selected after observing R3/R4 one-hour diagnostics

claims.tested_object: bounded comparative screen of 4h/12h/24h forward-return accessibility against the 1h reference using the same N0 features and ridge probe

estimand.primary: for each candidate horizon: February Pearson correlation, true-minus-median-shuffle correlation, and paired correlation gain over 1h reference under common resamples
estimand.candidate_rule: all three one-sided bootstrap lower bounds > 0; among eligible horizons choose highest point true correlation, tie to shorter horizon
estimand.unit: dependence-aware 48h moving blocks over the common February hourly sequence

claims.estimator: January-standardized closed-form ridge(lambda=1), February Pearson correlation, eight matched shuffled-January-target controls, paired circular moving-block bootstrap
claims.replication_unit: 48h circular moving block; 4096 bootstrap replicates are uncertainty draws, not independent scientific replicates
validity_prerequisites: same common decision timestamps for all horizons
targets remain inside Jan-Feb allowed archives
same N0 features/standardizer/ridge lambda across horizons
no February fitting or horizon selection during training
credible_alternatives: apparent horizon gain from sample-window differences is controlled by common timestamps
apparent relation from target leakage is controlled by causal target construction
apparent predictability from fitting noise is characterized by shuffled-January-target controls
screening multiplicity remains unresolved and therefore requires a new follow-up experiment
authority_scope: may prioritize one screened horizon as a candidate for a new formal follow-up
may conclude that none of the screened longer horizons earned screening promotion

screen.target_formula: close[first_consequence_hour + h - 1] / open[first_consequence_hour] - 1.0; N0 state uses only the 64 represented hours strictly before first_consequence_hour
screen.feature_standardization: January common-fit mean/population-std; drop std<=1e-12; freeze for February
screen.candidate_selection: eligible horizon with highest point true correlation; exact tie selects shorter horizon

uncertainty_protocol.method: paired circular moving-block bootstrap over common February hourly indices
